NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is to install a hydrophilic silica desiccant cartridge in the anode recirculation loop to locally humidify the anode gas stream during high-current operation. Standard practice uses continuous cathode humidification to maintain membrane hydration; this intervention shifts humidification duty to the anode side during high-current operation via a passive moisture-scavenging mechanism, using a commercially available desiccant material that releases moisture when exposed to anode exhaust gas. The closest existing practice is using desiccant dryers in fuel cell systems to remove moisture, but here we repurpose the desiccant as a moisture reservoir to actively humidify the anode gas, a reversal of its conventional function. The mechanism attacks the driving variable of anode-side gas dryness, which exacerbates membrane dehydration by reducing the chemical potential gradient for water back-diffusion from the cathode.

PHYSICS CHECK
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = anode gas relative humidity; the mechanism moves it UP by 15-20% absolute via moisture release from the desiccant; this REDUCES the membrane dehydration rate. The governing relation is the water back-diffusion flux from cathode to anode: J_w = D_w * (Δc_w / δ), where D_w is the water diffusivity in the membrane, δ is the membrane thickness, and Δc_w is the concentration gradient. By increasing anode humidity, the anode-side water concentration (c_w,a) rises, narrowing Δc_w = c_w,c - c_w,a and thus reducing the net water loss from the membrane. Magnitude verification: a commercial silica desiccant (e.g., type 3A molecular sieve) can release 0.2-0.3 g water per gram of desiccant when exposed to 80% RH gas at 80°C. For a 1 kW stack operating at 1.5 A/cm², anode flow is ~0.5 SLPM, requiring ~0.05 g/min additional water to maintain 80% RH—achievable with a 10g desiccant cartridge cycling between adsorption/desorption.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- Standard practice: continuous cathode humidification (stated equipment)
- Intervention: Install hydrophilic silica desiccant cartridge in anode recirculation loop
  - (b) Commercial 3A molecular sieve desiccant cartridge, 20g capacity, 1/4" NPT ports (stock item from industrial gas drying suppliers)
  - (c) Relocate existing anode recirculation pump outlet line through desiccant cartridge (no hardware change, just reroute tubing)
  - (c) Set desiccation duty cycle: 30 min adsorption (high-current phase) / 90 min desorption (low-current phase) using existing stack controller timer
  - (c) Adjust anode recirculation flow rate to 1.0 SLPM (from standard 0.5 SLPM) using existing control valve to enhance moisture transport

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installation: Desiccant cartridge installation (b) replaces humidifier maintenance; same labor class (pipe fitting, valve adjustment)
- Commissioning: Timer programming (c) uses existing controller; no new training
- Operation: Desiccant cartridge (b) has 6-month lifespan (same as standard humidifier filter); no added operator burden
- Maintenance: Same quarterly inspection schedule as standard practice; cartridge swap (b) is same labor class as filter replacement
- Cost: Desiccant cartridge (b) costs $25/unit (same as standard humidifier filter); no net increase
- Operational loss: Zero—duty cycle uses existing low-current windows (e.g., startup/shutdown) when parasitic load is already minimal

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run two identical stacks at 1.5 A/cm²/80°C, one with continuous cathode humidification (standard), one with desiccant humidification intervention. Monitor membrane resistance via in-stack impedance spectroscopy and stack temperature distribution via embedded thermocouples. Duration: 500 hours of continuous operation. Pass/fail: Intervention stack shows <5% increase in membrane resistance and <2°C localized temperature rise vs. standard stack. Kill criterion: If intervention stack resistance increases >10% or temperature exceeds standard by >5°C, test fails and mechanism is rejected.
